The Windows distribution dynamically links unmodified Qt libraries supplied by
The Qt Company: Qt Core, Gui, Widgets, Network, Qml, Quick, Positioning,
WebChannel and WebEngine (including Chromium and its third-party components).

Qt 6.10.2 source: https://download.qt.io/archive/qt/6.10/6.10.2/single/
Module repositories and the matching tag v6.10.2:
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtbase.git/
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtdeclarative.git/
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtwebchannel.git/
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtwebengine.git/
https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtpositioning.git/

Qt modules are used under their open-source license terms, with license texts
included here. Chromium and third-party credits are included in Qt WebEngine
and in its matching source archive (src/3rdparty/chromium/LICENSE and credits).
You may replace the Qt DLLs with compatible builds; this application does not
perform binary signature checks or prevent relinking against modified Qt.
No Qt source modifications were made. Application source is supplied alongside
the installer and is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later (desktop-native/third_party/
telegramdesktop/LICENSE). The QR generator retains its MIT license in its header.
Microsoft runtime libraries, where deployed, retain Microsoft's license terms.
